title: Unconverged circular-reference cached values in gt_07_golden.xlsx and un-recalculated GT comparison make the task impossible to pass
evidence: The sole verifier `SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check` (`verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells`, weight 1.0) force-recalculates the submitted `output_path` in LibreOffice (`managed_recalculated_xlsx(Path(output_path), force_recalculation=True)`), but loads `gt_path` (`gt_07_golden.xlsx`) and `reference_path` (`untouched_input_Double Counting_input.xlsx`) directly from their raw cached values on disk without recalculating them. In `LBO & Lenders` columns S:X, rows 49–53 form an iterative circular debt-schedule loop (`T50 = T53 - T52`, `T51 = SUM(T49:T50)`, `T53 = T54 * AVERAGE(T49, T51)`). None of those formulas change between the input and golden workbooks (only row 44 `S44:X44` changes to remove double counting, which does not feed into rows 49–59). However, `gt_07_golden.xlsx` stores stale, unconverged cached values in `T49:X59` that violate its own formulas (e.g., `T53` is cached as `118.970238303129`, whereas `T54 * AVERAGE(T49, T51) = 0.1275 * AVERAGE(938.685564032242, 931.191189540738) = 119.204643040277`, and the true fixed-point converged value is `119.2206038435`). When `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` is run on `gt_07_golden.xlsx` itself as `output_path`, LibreOffice recalculates the circular loop toward the true fixed point and the golden workbook fails against itself with `score=0.0` (`regression 1.0000, modification 0.8922, 17 cell error(s)`, e.g. `LBO & Lenders!T50: answer=-7.49437449150413, output=-7.25996975435565`, `V53: answer=115.422659476154, output=116.933385709013`, `X51: answer=880.681980565791, output=889.808311440059`). Any workbook saved with live formulas in `LBO & Lenders!T49:X59` is force-recalculated by the verifier and therefore cannot match the unconverged cached values in `gt_07_golden.xlsx`.
confirmation: Confirmed by local replay: the GT cached circular values (e.g. V53 115.42 vs recalculated 116.93) do not survive LibreOffice recalculation, so no live-formula workbook can match and the sole check is unpassable.
fix: Replaced gt_07_golden.xlsx and the reference workbook with copies recalculated through the verifier's LibreOffice path repeatedly (8 passes) until the circular interest/debt block in LBO & Lenders converged; the converged values match the closed-form fixed point (e.g. T50 -7.244, X50 -12.072, formulas unchanged). The new golden scores 1.0 against itself, and so does a workbook whose caches are one LibreOffice pass from converged. Residual risk (infra): an output saved with no cached values (e.g. plain openpyxl) still does not converge in the verifier's single LibreOffice pass.

title: The golden workbook fails its own verifier after mandatory recalculation

title: Golden gate: the ground-truth deliverable does not score full reward
evidence: The ground-truth deliverable, staged at the verifiers' own output paths and graded by the problem's real grader, scored 0.00 (need >= 1.00). A correct answer that does not earn full reward means a verifier false-negatives the mandated work. With the ground truth staged, every one of the 1 checks on /home/model/Desktop/output.xlsx scored 0 (summed weight 1.000), which is the whole shortfall of the GT grade. A correct deliverable does not fail every check at once; the ground truth for this file most likely never reached the grader (paired with a file of another type or name), so these are not 1 separate verifier defects. Checks: SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check.
confirmation: Reproduced locally: verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells on gt_07_golden.xlsx itself returns 0.0 (regression 1.0, modification 0.8922, 17 errors in 'LBO & Lenders' T50:X59, e.g. T50 -7.494 vs -7.260).

title: SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check: verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells fails correct solutions (score 0.0 on units 1 and 2, and on the golden file itself) because it force-recalculates output_path but compares against unconverged cached values in gt_07_golden.xlsx
evidence: Across the workbook, there are exactly 16 double-counting formulas that differ between `untouched_input_Double Counting_input.xlsx` and `gt_07_golden.xlsx`: `'BS & CF'!F30:G30` (`=SUM(F24:F29)+F25` -> `=SUM(F24:F29)`), `'DCF Model'!G99:L99` (`=SUM(G93:G98)+G94` -> `=SUM(G93:G98)`), `'LBO & Lenders'!S44:X44` (`=SUM(S39:S43)+S40` -> `=SUM(S39:S43)`), and `'Equity Returns'!D60,I60` (`=SUM(D58:D59)+D58` -> `=SUM(D58:D59)`). Both Unit 1 (steps [26]-[51]) and Unit 2 (steps [40]-[57]) identified and fixed all 16 double-counting formulas identically to the golden workbook while leaving all other cells intact. However, both Unit 1 and Unit 2 scored `0.0` (`regression 1.0000, modification 0.8922. 17 cell error(s)`) with every single error in the circular debt schedule `'LBO & Lenders'!T50:X59` (e.g., Unit 1 `T50: answer=-7.49437449150413, output=-7.24400895115832`; Unit 2 `T50: answer=-7.49437449150413, output=-7.36171037305418`). Even passing `gt_07_golden.xlsx` itself to `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` yields `score=0.0` with the exact same 17 cell errors (`regression 1.0000, modification 0.8922`), because `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` runs `managed_recalculated_xlsx(Path(output_path), force_recalculation=True)` on the submission while reading raw, unconverged cached values from `gt_07_golden.xlsx`.
confirmation: The verifier recalculates only the output, while the GT's circular debt block in 'LBO & Lenders' keeps unconverged caches. The golden file reproduces the same 17 errors and score 0, so correct double-counting fixes also fail.
fix: Replaced gt_07_golden.xlsx and the reference workbook with copies recalculated through the verifier's LibreOffice path repeatedly (8 passes) until the circular interest/debt block in LBO & Lenders converged; the converged values match the closed-form fixed point (e.g. T50 -7.244, X50 -12.072, formulas unchanged). The new golden scores 1.0 against itself, and so does a workbook whose caches are one LibreOffice pass from converged. Residual risk (infra): an output saved with no cached values (e.g. plain openpyxl) still does not converge in the verifier's single LibreOffice pass.
